name: Hooky
short: Send page context to webhooks with clear feedback, reusable templates, and optional headers and receipts. A product of hexly.ai.
headline: Your page. In motion.
summary: Capture a link, a selection, or a note for your own webhook. See the result, and add the options your endpoint needs.
description:
Hooky — Your page. In motion.

Send a link to your reading list, capture a selection for your knowledge system, or trigger your own workflow without leaving Chrome. You choose the webhook. Hooky brings the page context.

WHAT'S NEW IN 2.1

Clearer feedback comes to every send: the popup, Quick Send, and the right-click menu share request states, persistent toolbar badges, and a latest-result panel for the browser session. Page feedback makes results easier to notice. Open the panel or latest result without triggering another Quick Send rule. Identical requests already in progress share one send.

Configure advanced capabilities separately for each webhook: custom request headers, a send UUID, a small response receipt, JSON fields and a business success condition, and a warning for recently completed duplicate requests. These options stay off until configured.

MAKE A TEMPLATE. USE IT AGAIN.

Save a name, endpoint, HTTP method, and key-value parameters. GET and DELETE use query parameters; POST, PUT, and PATCH send a JSON object with string values. Review the request before sending.

Optional headers support Authorization, X-API-Key, and Idempotency-Key. Values stay masked in previews. Content-Type remains application/json; browser-managed headers cannot be overridden. Requests with custom headers do not follow redirects.

BRING THE PAGE WITH YOU

Use these variables in parameter or header values:

• {{page.url}} — page URL
• {{page.title}} — page title
• {{page.selection}} — selected text
• {{page.meta.description}} — description metadata
• {{page.meta.og:title}} — Open Graph title
• {{page.meta.og:description}} — Open Graph description
• {{page.meta.og:image}} — Open Graph image URL
• {{send.id}} — one UUID shared by the headers and parameters of a logical send

Review resolved values in the popup. Type or paste multiline notes without changing the saved template. Edited text keeps whitespace, line breaks, and literal {{...}} syntax. Pasting never sends automatically.

KNOW WHAT THE RECEIVER SAID

Optional response reading retains up to 8 KiB of text or JSON, for up to 3 seconds after HTTP headers arrive. Receipts appear as plain text only inside Hooky and last for the browser session. Map JSON message and receipt fields or require an exact JSON scalar value as a business success condition.

HTTP success alone does not prove durable storage. Lost responses remain unconfirmed; Hooky does not retry automatically. A send UUID enables receiver-supported idempotency; the receiver must implement it.

Completed duplicate protection is optional per webhook, with a 1–300 second window. A repeated request shows the previous result. Review the held capture and choose Send anyway to send it again with a new UUID. The capture is available briefly in background memory and disappears when the worker stops.

ONE CLICK WHEN THE PAGE MATCHES

Quick Send rules choose a template on your toolbar click. Match page URL or title using contains, equals, starts with, ends with, or a regular expression. Matching ignores case. Enable or disable rules, test a sample, and set priority. The first enabled matching rule with a valid template sends; otherwise the popup opens. Rules do not send automatically as you browse.

Templates also appear in the Hooky context menu. Choose one to send page context or selected text. Optionally enable desktop notifications for errors and unconfirmed outcomes, or for all results. Notifications show only the template name and generic status.

SMALL BY DESIGN

Native JavaScript and local assets. No account, analytics, publisher relay, or cloud sync. Templates, headers, rules, and preferences stay in local browser storage. Page context is read on demand; requests go to your endpoint. Session results and opted-in receipts clear when Chrome clears the extension session. The receiving service controls data after delivery.

SET UP IN A MINUTE

1. Open Settings and create a webhook template.
2. Enter your endpoint, method, and parameters.
3. Add page variables and any optional endpoint settings, then save.
4. Open a webpage, review the values, and send.

You provide a compatible webhook or automation endpoint. Hooky does not provide service accounts or full-page text extraction.

Available in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Russian. The interface follows Chrome's language. Requires Chrome 127 or later. Existing templates and rules remain compatible.

release:
Hooky 2.1.0

• Clear feedback across popup, Quick Send, and context-menu sends, with persistent badges and session results.
• Shared protection for identical requests already in progress; no automatic replay after interruption.
• Optional custom headers, masked previews, and a shared {{send.id}} UUID.
• Optional bounded text/JSON receipts, JSON fields, and typed business success rules.
• Optional completed duplicate protection and explicit Send anyway.
• Type or paste multiline notes without changing the saved template or sending automatically.
• Optional desktop notifications with permission recovery controls.
• Preserve literal edited values and GET/DELETE query parameters, including URLs with fragments.
• Existing templates and rules remain compatible; all 10 interface languages are updated.
• Requires Chrome 127 or later. Desktop notifications use an optional permission, requested when enabled in Settings.

A product of hexly.ai.
purpose: Send user-configured webhook requests with page context or explicitly entered text, using reusable templates and optional click-triggered matching rules, and report the outcome.
permissions:
activeTab
Reads the active page URL and title after a user gesture and authorizes on-demand selection and metadata access. Used by the popup, Quick Send, and context menu.

scripting
Extracts page context on demand and displays generic feedback after a triggered send. No persistent content script runs on navigation. Feedback excludes captured text, credentials, and receipts.

storage
Uses chrome.storage.local for templates, custom headers, rules, theme, and notification preferences. Uses chrome.storage.session for send summaries, opted-in bounded receipts, and optional recent duplicate fingerprints. No cloud sync.

contextMenus
Lists configured templates and provides separate Preview send and Latest send actions that do not trigger a Quick Send rule.

notifications (optional)
Shows generic desktop feedback only after the user enables a notification preference and grants permission from Settings. Off by default. Notifications contain only template name and status.

Host permissions: <all_urls>
Allows cross-origin HTTP/HTTPS requests to arbitrary endpoints explicitly configured by the user, including endpoints without browser CORS support. Domains cannot be known at installation. Hooky does not crawl tabs or send browsing activity to the publisher.
data:
Publisher collection: none. No analytics, advertising, account, relay, cloud sync, or remote executable code.
Local storage: template names, endpoints, parameters, custom headers, rules, theme, and notification preferences. Values may include credentials or personal information. Headers are masked in previews; local storage is not a password vault.
Session storage: latest send metadata and outcome; bounded response text only when enabled. Optional duplicate protection stores request fingerprints and summaries. Raw request bodies and credentials are not stored in duplicate history.
Temporary captures: explicit repeats can use original captures held only in worker memory, up to 20 captures for at most 60 seconds or until the worker stops.
Website content: URL/title, selected text, description, and Open Graph fields are read on demand. Configured variables determine what is sent. Manually entered or pasted text is sent only by a subsequent send action.
Clipboard: Hooky does not request clipboard permissions or read the clipboard programmatically. Users can paste into parameter fields using standard browser controls.
Browsing data: no ongoing navigation history is recorded. Active page URL/title may be included in a triggered request.
Destinations: user-configured endpoints. Custom-header requests refuse redirects; other requests use browser redirect handling. Receivers can see normal network metadata such as IP address.
Feedback: page and optional desktop feedback show only template name and generic status. Opted-in receipts remain inside Hooky and may contain sensitive content returned by the receiver.
Purpose: perform the webhook action chosen by the user. No sale, advertising use, or credit/lending use of data.
Deletion: delete templates/rules or uninstall to remove local data. Session data clears on browser restart or extension reload, update, or disable. Previously delivered data must be managed at the receiver.
